title: Adaptive Degradation Safety & Verification Manual (2025)
body:
Summary:

This manual sets out the safety contracts, verification checks, benchmark protocols and runbooks used to validate adaptive degradation and fallback in the Redwood serving runtime. It is for runtime engineers, SREs and release owners who gate runtime and scheduler changes, and brings architecture contracts, harnesses, profiling, acceptance criteria and incident steps into one place.

Scope:
- Adaptive degradation (fidelity staircases, model-variant fallback, burst shedding) and its interaction with the scheduler and kernels.
- Verification in CI, pre-release staging and canary.
- Profiling and benchmarking for SLO verification and regression detection.
- On-call and release-owner runbooks for rollback and mitigation.

Safety principles:
1) Observable: each degradation path emits metrics, traces or events and carries a single trace ID for forensic replay.
2) Fail open vs fail closed: enterprise-configured correctness-critical requests fail closed; latency-sensitive, non-critical requests may fail open to keep throughput.
3) Bounded fidelity loss: each step degrades quality predictably (measured on eval sets) and can be reversed.
4) Deterministic rollback: automated fallbacks expose a deterministic rollback path with human-confirmable guardrails.

Architecture contracts:
- Tiers: primary (full model), degraded-1 (quantized), degraded-2 (short-context variant), fallback (smaller model / cached embeddings), each with an SLO budget and cost profile.
- Kernel scheduling: the scheduler keeps per-request kernel affinity for the first N tokens and preserves KV cache affinity during tier transitions (default N=8).
- Eviction and warmup: after KV cache eviction, a configurable warmup window (default 60s) is reserved to rehydrate frequent prompts without hurting SLOs.

Verification matrix:
| Check ID | Purpose | Where executed | Acceptance threshold | Action on fail | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| VD-01 | End-to-end tail latency vs 95th percentile SLO | CI staging + canary | p95 < 1500ms for interactive path | block release, auto-rollback in canary | runtime-sre |
| VD-02 | Hot kernel latency jitter | perf-lab | 95th/50th ratio < 3.0 | throttle scheduling + revert kernel flags | runtime-kernel-team |
| VD-03 | Fidelity regression on golden prompts | automated evals | task metric delta < 1.5% | fail gating | applied-ml |
| VD-04 | KV cache hitrate during warmup | synthetic replay | hitrate > 70% after 120s | cached-response fallback | runtime-sre |
| VD-05 | Fallback routing correctness | chaos lab | 0 dropped requests during switch | incident | runtime-oncall |

Artifacts per check: replay corpus snapshot (sha256), expected telemetry schemas and trace samples, and baseline benchmark outputs for diff gating.

Harnesses:
1) CI unit stage: kernel microbenchmarks (latency, occupancy, memory) as fast-fail rules.
2) Staging perf run: full-stack replay of sampled production traffic (1:1000) with degraded-tier injection, producing histogram dumps, kernel traces and KV cache heatmaps.
3) Canary: A/B model variants with automated rollback on any VD-* failure and health checks every 5m.

Benchmarking protocol:
- Workloads:
  - Interactive short-chat (mean 40 tokens, 90th 128): low-latency SLOs.
  - Streaming long-output (mean 800 tokens): throughput and memory stability.
  - Embeddings burst (large batches): batching efficiency and memory.
- Metrics: end_to_end_latency_ms (p50/p90/p95/p99), per-kernel kernel_exec_time_ms, gpu_mem_used_mb, kv_cache_hitrate_pct, tokens_per_second_per_gpu.
- Commands:
  - ./perf-runner --profile=replay --corpus=sha256:abcd1234 --duration=15m --out=artifacts/replay-$(date +%s).tgz
  - python tools/microbench.py --kernel matmul --batch 1 --seq 128 --out json --repeat 50
  - curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $CI_TOKEN" https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"<<golden>>"}' -o /tmp/trace.json
- Acceptance:
  - No p95 regression > 10% vs baseline.
  - Kernel jitter (95/50) <= 3.0.
  - Less than 5% KV cache hitrate loss after warmup.

Profiling:
1) Latency fingerprints on a perf-lab host: export PERF_SAMPLER=on; ./runtime --enable-tracing --trace-sample-rate=0.01; run 10 minutes; tar -czf traces.tgz /var/tmp/traces/*; python tools/trace-aggregate.py --input traces.tgz --output traces-summary.json
2) Kernel causality: annotate kernels with request-id and token-index via the kernel-hint exporter; hotpaths: sum(rate(kernel_exec_time_ms_bucket[5m])) by (kernel_name)
3) Attribution checklist: tie p95 skew to a kernel or queue time in the trace waterfall; check GPU utilization and evictions; correlate KV cache misses with affinity changes.

Incident triage runbook:
1) Detection: alert on p95 or error-rate breaching the matrix thresholds.
2) First 10 min (oncall-runtime): compare dashboards to baseline; rate(request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m]) by (route); runtimectl list-sessions --filter=evicted=true --since=10m
3) Containment (10–30 min):
  - Kernel regression: runtimectl kernel-set active:stable-<tag> and pause canaries.
  - Warmup regression: set prewarm_multiplier=2 and send new sessions to degraded-1.
4) Remediation (30–90 min): roll back the config or kernel and validate with a quick replay; if still degraded, scale the dedicated pool for 15 minutes and collect artifacts.
5) All VD-* checks must pass in staging before automated rollouts resume.

Release gating checklist:
- Code owner review and ADR link.
- CI: unit tests, lint, kernel microbenchmarks.
- Perf artifacts: replay corpus, baseline histograms, guard thresholds.
- Canary health checks and thresholds attached.
- Rollback plan and named approvers in the release ticket.

Metrics schema:
- runtime.request.latency_ms, runtime.kernel.exec_ms, runtime.kv.hits, runtime.fidelity.tier, runtime.eviction.count
- Tags: service, model_name, model_variant, route, region, canary_id
- Trace fields: request_id, session_id, token_index, kernel_name, warmup_phase

Ownership and escalation:
- Runtime architecture: runtime-arch@redwood.ai (Sanjay Rao).
- Kernel scheduling: kernel-team@redwood.ai.
- Oncall: runtime-sre.
- Escalation: oncall -> SRE lead -> runtime-arch -> Eng Director (timed escalation at 60m).

Appendix A — degradation policy (fleet config)

  degradation_policy:
    tiers:
      - name: primary
        model_variant: v2-full
        slos:
          p95_latency_ms: 900
      - name: degraded-1
        model_variant: v2-quantized
        slos:
          p95_latency_ms: 700
      - name: degraded-2
        model_variant: v2-shortctx
        slos:
          p95_latency_ms: 350
    warmup:
      kv_cache_warmup_seconds: 120
      prewarm_multiplier: 1.5
    fallback:
      strategy: route-to-smaller-model
      max_inflight_fallback: 250

Appendix B — PromQL
- p95 by route: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(runtime_request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
- Jitter index: p95 over p50 of kernel_exec_time_ms_bucket by kernel.

Appendix C — reproducing regressions
1) Snapshot the failing commit and baseline artifacts.
2) Run perf-runner with the failing kernel flag and baseline corpus.
3) Collect traces.tgz and microbench outputs.
4) Upload to /artifacts/regressions/<ticket-id>.

Change log:
- 2025-08-04: Initial version with verification matrix (S. Rao).
- 2025-11-18: Added profiling playbook and triage runbook (E. Hart).

For any new scheduler or kernel change: add microbench checks, register baselines, run the staging replay, pass VD-* checks, canary, and be ready to roll back.
